system_description.narrative_title: War, Oil and Markets: A Fraying Global Order
system_description.narrative_summary: A cluster of regional wars (notably U.S.–Iran and Russia–Ukraine) and maritime seizures by Iran-aligned Houthis are choking shipping lanes and driving oil above $100, transmitting an energy shock through inflation, bond markets and central-bank policy. Simultaneously, assertive U.S. trade and domestic political moves, rising European far-right gains, and renewed great-power competition (Russia, China, North Korea) are amplifying fragmentation across trade, finance and security networks. The system is an open, tightly coupled global political‑economic process where shocks in one domain (security) rapidly propagate into markets, supply chains and domestic politics elsewhere.
system_description.scope: Major-state foreign policy and military conflicts; global energy and maritime security (oil, chokepoints, tankers); international financial markets (bonds, FX, central banks); trade rules and industrial policy (tariffs, export surpluses); regional political shifts in Europe and allies' domestic politics — roughly the set of actors and processes shaping geopolitics and the global economy today.
system_description.super_system: The integrated global political‑economic order (multilateral institutions, interconnected markets, global supply chains and security architectures).
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy & maritime security (oil markets, chokepoints, shipping)
International financial markets & central banking (bond yields, FX, inflation policy)
Regional security clusters (Middle East, Eastern Europe/Ukraine, East Asia)
Global trade and industrial supply chains (tariffs, export flows, strategic minerals)

variables.name: Maritime chokepoint security crisis
variables.description: Iran-backed proxies, Gulf states and external navies are contesting the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el‑Mandeb, shifting maritime security toward recurrent attacks that imperil seaborne trade and crude flows.

variables.name: Russia‑Ukraine high‑intensity war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in sustained high‑intensity conflict with cross‑border strikes and episodic escalation that are entrenching a prolonged war of attrition and complicating regional security.

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are intensifying competition over semiconductors, AI supply chains, critical minerals and export controls, driving partial decoupling and a reordering of high‑tech trade rules.

variables.name: Global monetary and bond‑market stress
variables.description: A surge in government bond yields and a hawkish pivot by major central banks amid inflation surprises and policy uncertainty is reshaping global financing costs and fiscal dynamics.

variables.name: U.S. economic statecraft and trade coercion
variables.description: U.S. policymakers are increasingly deploying tariffs, import bans and financial instruments as instruments of foreign policy, shifting norms around economic coercion and bilateral commercial relations.
